reference.title: Kettlebell Alternating Press on Floor
reference.listing: Video (movement reference; the page could not be read at authoring time because the proxy blocked it, so the movement was taken from the exercise name and standard coaching)

breathing.pattern: Inhale as each bell lowers, exhale as it presses up.
breathing.cadence: About 1.4 s down, 0.3 s pause, 1.1 s up per arm

prescription.tempo: 1.4 s down, 0.3 s pause on the floor, 1.1 s up, alternating
prescription.load: Kettlebell load is user-chosen: pick bells you can hold locked out for the whole set with 1-3 reps in reserve.
prescription.progression: Add reps, then heavier bells; then pause 2 s with one arm down.

cues.text: Lie on the mat, knees bent and feet flat; both kettlebells pressed up over the chest, palms toward the feet, wrists straight.
Breathe in and lower the right bell, elbow about 45 degrees from the side, forearm vertical, while the left arm stays locked out.
Upper arm rests on the floor for a moment.
Breathe out and press it back up beside the other bell.
Now lower the left bell the same way; the right stays up.
Press the left back up; keep the hips and ribs still throughout.
Both arms straight over the chest; go again.

mistakes.mistake: Elbows flared straight out at 90 degrees
mistakes.fix: Bring the elbows to about 45 degrees from the body so the upper arms land on the floor angled toward the hips.

mistakes.mistake: Bouncing the elbows off the floor
mistakes.fix: Touch the floor softly, pause for a moment, then press.

mistakes.mistake: Wrists bent back, kettlebells drifting toward the face
mistakes.fix: Keep the forearms vertical and the wrists straight.

mistakes.mistake: Bridging the hips up to press
mistakes.fix: Keep the glutes on the floor; drive through the feet only to brace.
Press up and slightly in, stopping a few centimetres apart.

kinematics.norm: Arms straight but not locked at the top; at the bottom the upper arms rest on the floor with the elbows at about 90 degrees (clinical opinion)

kinematics.measure: Elbow flare (upper arm from the trunk)
kinematics.norm: About 45 degrees from the body when the upper arm touches the floor (clinical opinion)
Back of the upper arm rests briefly on the floor at the bottom (clinical opinion)
The other arm stays straight over the shoulder while one bell is lowered (alternating press; clinical opinion)
Feet flat, knees bent about 70-90 degrees (clinical opinion)
About 2 s down, a short pause with the arms on the floor, 1-1.5 s up (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual 13771, Kettlebell Alternating Press on Floor, video (movement reference)

cautions: Get into position safely: lie down with one bell at a time pulled to the chest with both hands, and at the end of the set bring each bell back to the chest and roll it off to the side, never dropping it over the face (clinical opinion).
Let the upper arms touch the floor softly; do not bang the elbows down or bounce off the floor.
Keep the wrists straight over the forearms.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Shoulder discomfort: neutral grip (palms facing each other) and elbows tucked closer.
Lower back discomfort: bring the feet a little closer to the hips.

muscleNotes.pec_r: Main pusher (horizontal adduction and flexion of the upper arm). The floor stops the elbows at about body level, so the stretched bottom of a bench press is left out (clinical opinion); with kettlebells, pectoralis activity matched barbell and Smith machine presses (Saeterbakken 2011).
muscleNotes.pec_l: Main pusher (horizontal adduction and flexion of the upper arm). The floor stops the elbows at about body level, so the stretched bottom of a bench press is left out (clinical opinion); with kettlebells, pectoralis activity matched barbell and Smith machine presses (Saeterbakken 2011).
muscleNotes.triceps_r: Straightens the elbows; with the range shortened to the upper part, the lockout share is relatively larger (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Straightens the elbows; with the range shortened to the upper part, the lockout share is relatively larger (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Flexes the shoulder with the chest.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Flexes the shoulder with the chest.
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Holds the shoulder blades against the rib cage while each arm moves on its own.
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Holds the shoulder blades against the rib cage while each arm moves on its own.
muscleNotes.biceps_r: Stabilises the elbow; biceps activity rose with the stability demand and was highest with kettlebells (Saeterbakken 2011).
muscleNotes.biceps_l: Stabilises the elbow; biceps activity rose with the stability demand and was highest with kettlebells (Saeterbakken 2011).
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Grip the handle; the offset bell pulls the wrist back (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Grip the handle; the offset bell pulls the wrist back (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: Rotator cuff: centres the head of the upper arm while the kettlebells balance freely (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_l: Rotator cuff: centres the head of the upper arm while the kettlebells balance freely (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Keep the shoulder blades drawn back and down on the floor.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Keep the shoulder blades drawn back and down on the floor.
muscleNotes.core: Stops the trunk rolling toward the working side while one bell is down (clinical opinion).
